messages:
Aisha: Heads-up: enterprise pilot (DeltaHealth) asked for strict SLA before they go live. They want 99.9% availability for inference endpoints. Can we realistically commit for MVP?
Marco: Short answer: not without dedicating capacity and the reliability work. We can hit 99.9% in Dedicated but not in hosted at current infra.
Leah: If we make SLA a hard blocker, we must push prompt UX and analytics to v1. That reduces launch surface but delays value for freemium users.
Tom: Alternative: offer SLA as an add-on (private/dedicated) for pilot customers. Define clear checklist for Dedicated onboarding instead of changing MVP.
Aisha: DeltaHealth prefers single-plan simplicity; they'd rather we include SLA in the product path. They can commit $$ if we can give a go/no-go within 2 weeks.
Marco: Risk: rush reliability work -> fragile rollout. Suggest a scoped reliability bundle for MVP: > persistent warm pools, circuit-breakers, and SLO dashboard. Keep heavy autoscale improvements for v1.
Leah: Operational question: what are measurable acceptance criteria for that bundle? Need concrete metrics for the sales promise.
Tom: Proposal: Acceptance: 1) 99.5% availability over 7 days on canary traffic, 2) p99 latency < 800ms under baseline load, 3) documented rollback & runbook + oncall playbook.
Aisha: DeltaHealth wants 99.9 but might accept 99.5 for initial pilot if we timebox commitment and show roadmap to 99.9 by v1.
Marco: Ok can do 99.5 for pilot but we must require a dedicated capacity trial and signed SLA scope doc.
Leah: For roadmap, mark prompt UX as non-blocking for pilot; keep it targeted to early adopters only. Add a customer-facing feature flag so we can enable later.
Aisha: Action list: Marco -> scope infra bundle and cost estimate (due in 4 days). Leah -> flagging plan + minimal UX copy for pilot toggle (2 days). Tom -> draft SLA addendum + trial checklist (4 days). I'll coordinate with DeltaHealth and set expectation for go/no-go in 10 days.
Marco: Will put numbers in a PR to the release plan and tag @release-bot to schedule a canary once Delta signs.
release-bot: Canary scheduled: 5% traffic for 24h after dedicated capacity is provisioned. :calendar:
Aisha: Thanks, team. We should avoid broad scope creep; pilot-first SLA path seems safest. If Delta refuses the add-on, we'll need to decide if we shift the whole MVP.
Leah: noted. I'll make a visual in the milestone board showing two lanes: "Core MVP" and "Pilot SLA path" so stakeholders can see the divergence.
Tom: I'll draft the SLA language with explicit exit criteria and support windows.
Aisha: Cool — locking these action owners. If anyone finds a blocker, flag in this thread. :+1:
